note.text:
Settlement transactions pay or receive money owed:
• Customer pays by cheque or transfer: debit 521 Bank, credit 411 Customers. In cash: debit 571 Cash.
• Business pays a supplier: debit 401 Suppliers, credit 521 Bank (or 571 Cash).
• Moving money between cash and bank: cash paid into the bank: debit 521 Bank, credit 571 Cash (often through 585 Transfers of funds).
• Cash discount (escompte) for early payment: the seller records it as an expense (673 Discounts granted); the customer pays less.
The cash and bank accounts must never show impossible balances; cash in hand cannot be negative.

sections.heading: Settling debts
sections.text:
After a credit sale or purchase, someone still owes money. Settlement transactions pay these debts:
• A customer pays: debit {'521 Bank'} (cheque, transfer, mobile money to the business account) or {'571 Cash'}; credit {'411 Customers'}.
• The business pays a supplier: debit {'401 Suppliers'}; credit {'521 Bank'} or {'571 Cash'}.

sections.heading: Moving money and keeping it safe
sections.text:
Cash paid into the bank: debit {'521 Bank'}, credit {'571 Cash'}. Cash withdrawn from the bank: the reverse. Many businesses use a transfer account ({'585'}) between the two.
Keep track of the cash balance: opening cash + receipts − payments. It can never be negative: a credit balance on Cash shows an error.

sections.heading: Cash discounts
sections.text:
To be paid sooner, a seller may offer a cash discount (escompte): for example {2}% off if the customer pays within {10} days.
The customer pays less; the seller records the discount as an expense ({'673 Discounts granted'}), and the customer as income.
{100000} FCFA with a {2}% discount: the customer pays {98000} FCFA.

mistake.wrong: When a customer pays, credit Sales again
mistake.right: Credit {'411'} Customers: the sale was already recorded
mistake.why: Payment settles the debt; it is not a new sale.

worked_example.problem: Cash in hand is {open} FCFA. A customer pays {rec} FCFA in cash and a supplier is paid {pay} FCFA in cash. Find the new cash balance.
steps: Payments decrease it: {open + rec} − {pay} = {open + rec - pay} FCFA.

cards.idea: Money received from a customer: debit Bank or Cash, credit Customers.
Paying a supplier: debit Suppliers, credit Bank or Cash.

check.prompt: Cash in hand is {o} FCFA. During the day: cash sales {a} FCFA, a supplier paid {b} FCFA, {c} FCFA paid into the bank. What is the cash balance (FCFA)?

misconceptions.explain: Money paid into the bank leaves the cash box: subtract it.

cards.idea: A cash discount for early payment is an expense for the seller.

check.prompt: A customer owes {t} FCFA and pays early with a {d}% cash discount. How much does he pay (FCFA)?

misconceptions.explain: That is the discount, not the payment.

pick.q: A customer pays 150 000 FCFA by cheque, paid into the bank.
e: The sale was already recorded; now the debt is settled.
Not cash and not a supplier.
pick.y: Bank increases; the customer owes less.

pick.q: The business pays a supplier 90 000 FCFA by bank transfer.
e: The purchase was already recorded; now the debt is paid.
pick.y: The debt falls; the bank falls.

pick.q: 200 000 FCFA cash is paid into the bank.
e: That is withdrawing cash from the bank.
pick.y: Money moves from the till to the bank.

pick.q: Why can the cash account never have a credit balance?
pick.r: You cannot pay out more cash than is in the till
w: Credits are not allowed in accounting
pick.y: A credit balance on Cash means an error.

pick.q: Why do sellers offer cash discounts?
pick.r: To encourage customers to pay early
pick.y: Early payment improves the seller's cash flow.

pick.q: A cheque from a customer bounces (is unpaid). What should happen in the accounts?
pick.r: The entry is reversed: Dr 411 Customers / Cr 521 Bank
e: The bank did not receive the money.
That records it as received again.
pick.y: The customer still owes the money.
